title: Development of an AI-Based Virtual Camera Tracking System for Coarse Alignment of Mobile Free Space Optical Communication (FSOC) Terminals
department: Department of Space / Indian Space Research Organisation
description:
Background Free Space Optical Communication (FSOC) offers unprecedented advantages for next-generation mobile networks, including gigabit-to-terabit data rates, license-free spectrum operation, high immunity to electromagnetic interference, etc. However, deploying FSOC links between mobile platforms (satellites, UAVs presents a severe challenge of pointing, acquisition and tracking (PAT) of highly narrow laser beams. PAT typically happens in two stages: coarse alignment and fine alignment. Coarse alignment is one of the key challenges of PAT, where the transmitting terminal must first locate and maintain the remote terminal within its camera Field-of-View (FOV).
Developing and testing such algorithms on real hardware requires expensive cameras, pan-tilt mechanisms, and optical components & equipment. A software based virtual camera tracking provides an inexpensive and accessible platform for algorithm development and learning.
Description Unlike conventional radio-frequency systems, FSOC relies on a highly directional optical beam. Even a small angular error can prevent successful communication. Before fine pointing mechanism can take over, a coarse alignment stage must:
• Observe the surrounding environment,
• Acquire and detect the remote terminal or beacon,
• Estimate the position, and
• Continuously adjust the pointing direction to maintain visibility.
The participants shall develop this coarse alignment process in software, allowing to develop and validate tracking algorithms without specialized hardware and setup. The following section provides reference parameters and performance criteria to be considered for the software development.
Parameters and Specifications Functional Objective: Develop a software system that autonomously detects, identifies, and continuously tracks a designated moving target within a virtual scene by controlling a virtual camera viewport.
Add 'Parameters and Specifications' table here Expected Solution Participants shall develop an AI-assisted camera tracking system capable of automatically detecting and continuously tracking a moving optical beacon in a simulated video stream while controlling a virtual pan-tilt camera.
The developed software shall be able to:
• Generate a configurable virtual environment,
• Generate one or more moving targets,
• Implement a movable virtual camera,
• Detect the target beacon automatically,
• Track the beacon continuously using computer vision,
• Control and reposition the virtual camera,
• Generate and introduce disturbances due to atmospheric turbulence, platform vibrations, camera motion, noise, etc., in the virtual camera feed,
• Display tracking performance and statistics in real-time Deliverables Each participating team shall submit the following mandatory deliverables:
Software Application A standalone executable application implementing the complete virtual camera tracking system. The application shall provide all the mandatory functions and features as described above.
Source Code Complete source code with proper documentation. The code shall be modular and adequately commented.
Technical Report The technical report (about 10-15 pages) containing problem understanding, system architecture, description of software modules, tracking methods, AI methods (if used), test methodology, performance analysis and future improvements shall be submitted.
User Manual The user manual with the description of installation of software, application operation, parameter configuration, GUI description, etc. shall be submitted. A 3–5 minutes video may also be provided as an optional deliverable for demonstration of the application.
Performance Log The software should be capable of automatically generating a performance report containing simulation duration, FPS, acquisition time, average and maximum tracking error, lock retention rate, processing time, etc.
Evaluation Method and Criteria The solutions developed by participating teams will be evaluated using multi-layered evaluation method. The following table describes stages of evaluation, their weightage and methods.

Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. detail.title: Development of an AI-Based Virtual Camera Tracking System for Coarse Alignment of Mobile Free Space Optical Communication (FSOC) Terminals

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a software simulation of a camera-based tracking system that could locate and lock onto a moving optical communication terminal, the coarse alignment step needed before a narrow laser beam link can be established between satellites, drones, or other mobile platforms.
overview.why_it_matters: Testing real pointing-acquisition-tracking algorithms needs expensive cameras and pan-tilt hardware. A genuine software simulation platform makes this algorithm development accessible without that cost.
pain_points: Even a small angular error can prevent successful optical communication given how narrow FSOC laser beams are.
Developing and testing PAT algorithms on real hardware requires expensive cameras, pan-tilt mechanisms, and optical equipment.
No accessible, low-cost platform exists for developing and learning coarse-alignment tracking algorithms.
overview.background: FSOC's narrow optical beams require precise pointing-acquisition-tracking (PAT), but developing and testing coarse-alignment algorithms on real hardware is expensive, motivating a software-based virtual camera simulation.
overview.whats_being_asked: A software-based virtual camera tracking system simulating coarse alignment (target detection within camera field-of-view, tracking as platforms move) for mobile FSOC terminals.
expected_solution: Virtual camera simulation with realistic field-of-view constraints.
Target detection and tracking algorithm for simulated moving platforms.
Realistic simulation of mobile platform dynamics (satellite/UAV motion).

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Genuine simulated PAT algorithm development platform is a real, valuable contribution given the real cost barrier of physical hardware, technically substantial simulation and tracking-algorithm work.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate-high. Requires real simulation environment design (camera model, platform dynamics) plus genuine tracking algorithm implementation, substantial technical depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine understanding of both optical communication PAT concepts and computer vision tracking, a specialized combination.

innovation.note: A genuine, accessible simulation platform for a real, expensive-to-test problem is valuable technical contribution.

invention.note: Combining realistic camera/platform-motion simulation with genuine tracking algorithm implementation is substantial work.

technical_feasibility.note: This is explicitly a software-only, simulation-based task, no real hardware needed, genuinely achievable in 36 hours.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly enables lower-cost PAT algorithm development and learning, real value for a specialized research/engineering community.

architecture.note: A simulation environment plus tracking algorithm, well-understood pattern applied to this specific domain.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, explicitly software-only and simulation-based, removing hardware access barriers entirely. Ground your platform-motion and optical-physics simulation in real FSOC/satellite-tracking parameters to make it genuinely useful, not just a generic object-tracking demo.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Explicitly framed as a software simulation, no real optical hardware or pan-tilt mechanisms needed, fully achievable within 36 hours.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a generic object-tracking demo without genuine grounding in real FSOC coarse-alignment physics (field-of-view constraints, realistic platform motion/jitter) would miss the actual value of a purpose-built PAT development platform.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Research real FSOC coarse-alignment parameters (typical field-of-view sizes, realistic platform motion/jitter characteristics for satellites/UAVs) to ground your simulation in genuine domain accuracy, rather than a generic camera-tracking demo relabeled for this application.

idea_0_4: Research real FSOC coarse-alignment parameters and typical mobile-platform (satellite/UAV) motion characteristics.
Design your virtual camera model with realistic field-of-view constraints.
Split: one person on the simulation environment (camera model, platform dynamics), one on the tracking algorithm.
prototype_4_22: Build your virtual camera simulation with realistic FOV and platform-motion modeling.
Build your target detection and tracking algorithm within the simulated camera view.
Test tracking performance against various realistic platform motion scenarios.
integration_22_30: Connect simulation and tracking into one coherent, usable development platform.
Test with genuinely challenging scenarios (fast platform motion, target near FOV edge, realistic jitter/noise).
Add basic algorithm-development tooling (parameter tuning, performance metrics) to make this genuinely useful as a development platform.
polish_30_36: Polish the platform for genuine usability by someone developing/testing PAT algorithms.
Rehearse a live demo showing your tracking algorithm successfully maintaining lock on a simulated moving target.
Prepare to discuss your simulation's grounding in real FSOC/platform-motion parameters.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your tracking algorithm successfully maintaining coarse alignment against a genuinely challenging simulated scenario (fast platform motion, target approaching the FOV edge), with realistic FSOC-relevant parameters, and present basic performance metrics, that combination of realistic simulation grounding and demonstrated tracking robustness is what makes this a genuinely useful development platform, not just a tracking demo.

strengths: Explicitly software-only scope removes hardware access barriers entirely.
Genuine, valuable contribution to a real, expensive-to-test problem space.
weaknesses: Requires genuine FSOC/optical-communication domain research to be authentically useful, not generic.
Real platform motion characteristics (satellite/UAV) need research to simulate realistically.

team_fit.approach: Research real FSOC coarse-alignment and platform-motion characteristics before building your simulation, this grounding is what makes it genuinely useful versus generic.

data_resource_availability.status: No external dataset dependency, this is a simulation-construction task grounded in researched real FSOC/platform-motion parameters.

judge_qna.question: How realistic is your platform-motion simulation compared to actual satellite or UAV dynamics?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Cite the specific real motion characteristics (angular velocity ranges, typical jitter) you researched and incorporated into your simulation.
judge_qna.follow_up: What real-world dynamics might your simulation not fully capture?

judge_qna.question: How does your tracking algorithm perform under genuinely challenging conditions, not just easy, centered targets?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your test results against fast-motion or edge-of-FOV scenarios specifically, being honest about performance limits.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would happen to your algorithm's performance with realistic sensor noise added?
